title: Projective-bundle projectivity over an ample base implies H-projectivity
statement: Let $g:V\to S$ be projective in the EGA/ILO projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and suppose $S$ admits an ample invertible sheaf [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $g$ is H-projective, i.e. projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective].

proof.text: Unpack the projective-bundle hypothesis [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: there are a finite type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$ on $S$, the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)\to S$, and a closed immersion $i:V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ over $S$ with $g=\pi\circ i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to $\mathcal E$ and the ample invertible sheaf on $S$. Choosing a natural number $d$ at least the integer bound supplied there (and hence nonnegative) gives that $\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof: finite type module and ample twist; Properties Proposition Tag 01Q3

proof.text: The canonical relative-Proj twisting isomorphism [lem-trf-relative-proj-invertible-twist], applied with $\mathcal L$ and $d$, identifies $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ over $S$ with $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$.

By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-global-generated-h-projective], the projective-bundle morphism $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})\to S$ is H-projective because its module is generated by finitely many global sections. Transporting H-projectivity across the canonical isomorphism in Step 2 gives that $\pi$ is H-projective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof: the globally generated case and the preceding twisting paragraph

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is H-projective by the definition [def-kun-projective], taking the ambient projective space of dimension $0$ over $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ to be the base itself. Therefore the composition lemma [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] applied to $i$ and $\pi$ shows that $g=\pi\circ i$ is H-projective.
